Challenging the order dated 12.01.2022 passed by Commissioner for Employee's Compensation-2 (Joint Commissioner of Labour-2), Chennai made in E.C.No.230 of 2018.

2. On 03.09.2018 at about 6.10 p.m., the deceased namely Mr.Ramu, the husband of the first respondent, who was working as a Driver of the 4th respondent/lorry, after unloading the goods from the lorry and while parking the vehicle in fourth respondent's office, he died on the spot, due to sudden heart attack.
Hence, respondents 1 to 3, being the wife and daughter of the deceased made a claim for compensation under Section 30 of Workmen's Compensation Act,1923.
3. On consideration of oral and documentary evidence, the Commissioner for Employee's Compensation-2 (Joint Commissioner of Labour-2) has awarded a sum of Rs.8,94,376/- towards compensation.
Aggrieved by the said compensation amount, the appellant/Insurance Company has preferred the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis present appeal.

4. The only point for consideration arises in this appeal is, as to whether the death of the deceased was due to in an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment with the 4th respondent, which caused due to stress and strain of his employment?

5. The learned counsel for the appellant would contend that in the Post- Mortem report-Ex.P6, the Doctor opined that the deceased had passed away due to the Coronery Artery Disease (natural cause) and therefore, the workman died due to the natural cause and the Authority had not considered this aspect in proper perspective.

In support of his contention, he referred to Section 3 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 (in short 'the Act'), which is extracted hereunder:
"3. Employer's liability for compensation- (1) If personal injury is caused to a employee by accident arising out of and in the course of his employment, his employer shall be liable to pay compensation in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter:
(a) In respect of any injury which does not result in total or partial disablement of the employee for a period exceeding three days;
(b) in respect of any injury, not resulting in death [for permanent total disablement],
caused by] an https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis accident which is directly attributabe to- (i) the employee having been at the time thereof under the influence of dring or drugs, or The New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Mrs.Bavani on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157432880/
2 (ii) the wilful disobedience of the employee to an order expressly given, or to a rule expressly framed, for the purpose of securing the safety of employees, or (iii) the wilful removal or disregard by the employee of any safety guard or other device which he knew to have been provided for the purpose of securing the safety of employeees.

8. Heard the learned counsel appearing on either side and perused the records.
9.

In the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court (cited supra) relied on by the learned counsel for the Respondents 1 to 3, in para 22, the Hon'ble Supreme Court hold, that even a workman dies from a pre-existing disease, if the disease is aggravated or accelerated under the circumstances which can be said to be accidental, his death results from injury by accident.

The House of Lords in the case of Clover Claytan & Co. V. Hughes reported in 1910 AC 242 , it was held as follows:
"4. Even if a workman dies from a pre-existing disease, if a disease if aggravated or accelerated under the circumstances which can be said to be accidental, his death results from injury by accident.

entities.text: Clover Claytan & Co. V. Hughes reported in 1910 AC 242
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was clearly laid down by the House of Lords in Clover Clayton & Co. V. Hughes, where the deceased, whilest tightening a nut with a spanner, fell back on his hand and died.
A post mortem examination showed that there was a large https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis aneurism of the aorta, and that death was caused by repture of the aorta.
The aneurism was in such an advanced condition that it might have burst while the man was alsoeep, and very slight exertion or strain would have been sufficient to bring about a rupture.

The County Court Judge found that the death was caused by a strain arising out of the ordinary work of the deceased operating upon a condition of body which was such as to render the strain fatal, and held upon the authorities that this was an accident within the meaning of the Act.
His decision was upheld both by the Court of Appeal and House of Lords:

"No doubt the ordinary accident,"
said Lord Loreburn, L.C. "is accociated with something external: the bursting of a boiler or an explosion in a mine, for example.
But it may be merely from the man's own miscalcuation, such as tripping and falling.
Or it may be due both to internal and exernal conditions, as if a seaman were to faint in the rigging and tumble into the sea.
I think it may also be something going wrong within the human frame itself, such as straining of muscle or the breaking of a blood vessel.
If that occurred when he was lifting a weight, it would properly be described as an accident.
So, I think, rupturing an aneurism when tightening a nut with a spanner may be regarded as an accident."

With regard to Lord Macnanghten's definition of an accident being "an unlooked for mishap or untoward even which is not expected or designed" it was said that an event was unexpected if it was not expected by the man who suffered it, even though everyman of commonsense who knew the circumstances would think it certain to happen."

sentences.text: In the present case, it is not in dispute that the deceased while undertaking the job of driving as his regular avocation, there was every reason to assume that the avocation of driving was a material contributory factor that accelerated his unexpected death to occur which in all fairness, should be held to be an untoward mishap in his life span and such an untoward mishap can therefore be reasonably described as an accident and the same can be safely construed as solely attirubutable to the nature of employment indulged in with his employer.

11. Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this Court has no hesitation to hold that since the deceased during the course of his employment as a driver, due to the stress in his job suffered severe heart attack and died on the spot, while he was in the employment.
Thus, the death of the deceased was an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment with the 4th respondent.

Therefore, this Court does not find any infirmity or irregularity in the award granting compensation by the Commissioner of Employees Compensation-II and there is no scope to interfere with the same, by this Court.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 12.
Accordingly, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed as devoid of merits.

The appellant/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount before the Joint Commissioner of Labour-II, Chennai-6, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and on such deposit, the said authority is directed to permit the respondents 1 to 3 to withdraw the same.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
